title: US permitting reform plan could transform energy investment
gist: A bipartisan Senate group proposed the 417-page BAAJA to cap federal environmental decisions at two years, limit permit revocation and legal challenges, and make data centres pay for transmission they need. Wood Mackenzie says gas pipelines and transmission would gain most, but House Democrats signal no deal this year; the newsletter also covers a 100 million barrel G7 reserve release and diesel at about $185-195/bbl.

insights.claim: Four senators, two Republican and two Democratic, published the 417-page Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act to speed infrastructure permitting.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: A rare bipartisan vehicle for permitting reform; the key legislative event to track for US energy infrastructure.

insights.claim: BAAJA would limit federal environmental approval decisions to two years, restrain agencies from withdrawing granted permits, and restrict legal challenges to approvals.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Reduces timeline and legal risk, which would lower the cost of capital for pipelines, transmission and generation.
insights.quote: time limits of no more than two years for federal decisions on environmental approvals

insights.claim: A key provision would compel data centre developers to cover the cost of transmission investment needed to support their facilities.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Shifts grid-upgrade costs to AI data centre developers, affecting hyperscaler economics and easing cost allocation fights.

insights.claim: Surging AI data centre electricity demand has made permitting reform more urgent, and the bipartisan impetus is that the system hinders both fossil and low-carbon infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: AI power demand is the political lever breaking a decades-old permitting stalemate.

insights.claim: Passage this year looks unlikely: Rep. Jared Huffman said Democrats will not support a permitting bill until the new Congress, expecting midterm gains on 3 November.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Treat permitting-linked upside as a 2027 story; the midterm result sets the terms of any deal.
insights.quote: Folding our hand now… makes no sense when we can keep working on this and, in a few more months, have a much better deal.

insights.claim: US infrastructure builds routinely take decades: the Champlain Hudson Power Express took over 16 years, typical transmission lines take 15 to 20, and TransWest Express will take at least 26 years.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Quantifies the permitting drag that reform aims to remove.

insights.claim: Interstate gas pipeline capacity additions peaked in 2018 and high-voltage transmission additions in 2013, and both have stayed well below those levels despite growing need.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Shows how supply of grid and gas infrastructure lags AI-era demand.

insights.claim: US interstate gas pipeline capacity completed next year is expected to be the highest since 2018, helped by Trump executive orders and the Supreme Court's Seven County decision, but lasting change needs legislation.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Near-term pipeline pickup is executive-driven and reversible, so legislation matters for durability.
insights.quote: Next year, the capacity of interstate gas pipelines completed in the US is expected to be the highest since 2018.

insights.claim: If reform passes, Williams' Constitution Pipeline (proposed 2012) and Northeast Supply Enhancement (2017) could be early test cases for bringing Marcellus gas to New York.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Williams is the stock-specific beneficiary of a permitting law; Northeast gas pricing could ease.

insights.claim: The BAAJA could make a 'massive' difference to transmission by strengthening FERC, compelling joint regional planning, restricting utility blocking and creating a cost allocation framework.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Transmission is the binding constraint on data centre and renewables growth, so these provisions would unlock grid-equipment demand.

insights.claim: DOE announced US$1.9 billion for 31 projects under its SPARK reconductoring programme, a rebrand of a Biden-era programme, while scrapping three National Interest Electric Transmission Corridors in August.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Administration favours upgrading existing lines over new corridors, supporting reconductoring and advanced-conductor suppliers.

insights.claim: The G7 announced a 100 million barrel release from reserves over four months, about 830,000 barrels a day, front-loaded with substantial diesel releases in the first 20 days.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Policy response signals acute refined-product tightness and a cap on near-term diesel spikes.

insights.claim: November diesel in New York traded at about US$195 a barrel before the G7 announcement and about 5% lower at about US$185 after; US retail diesel averaged about US$6.37 a gallon, only 2% below a record set 10 days earlier.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Diesel remains near record levels despite the intervention.

insights.claim: Prices for refined products are being driven by the Middle East conflict and Russia's war with Ukraine and stay high despite increased Gulf oil flows, while Trump's suggestion of banning US diesel exports would push global prices up.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: A US diesel export ban is a tail risk for European diesel and refining margins.

insights.claim: South Korea's President Lee Jae Myung said no commitment has been made to Alaska LNG, conditional on commercial viability and Korean legal procedures, despite Trump framing it within a roughly US$200 billion investment package.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Alaska LNG financing remains uncertain, tempering expectations for the project.

insights.claim: Gas turbine orders outside China surged last year on AI-driven power investment, and strain on the supply chain means many large frame turbine orders will not be delivered until 2030.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Turbine makers hold pricing power and backlog visibility; delivery limits cap near-term power additions.

insights.claim: Governor Ron DeSantis's post 'Superintelligence factories = surveillance centers' signals political opposition to US data centre development may keep growing as Trump and Jensen Huang rebrand AI as 'superintelligence'.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Republican-side backlash raises local approval and political risk for data centre buildouts.
